name: Municipal socialism
summary: Municipal socialism uses elected local government to pursue socialist aims: taking gas, water, transport and similar services into public ownership, building public housing, funding health, school and welfare provision, and paying fair wages. It works gradually and democratically, through council elections and alliances with unions, co-operatives and tenant groups, and it often clashes with national governments that limit local powers.
scope: The reformist tradition from Chamberlain's Birmingham, the Fabians and the London County Council, through Poplarism, Red Vienna (1918-1934), Milwaukee 'sewer socialism' and the continental socialist councils, to the 1980s urban left. It excludes revolutionary Marxism, which Lenin counterposed to it, and answers for the mainstream democratic-socialist current. Many answers on issues outside local services are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Joseph Chamberlain
keyFigures.role: As mayor of Birmingham, municipalised gas and water, the origin of 'gas and water socialism'.

keyFigures.name: Sidney Webb
keyFigures.role: Fabian who described and promoted the spread of municipal services and sat on the London County Council.

keyFigures.name: George Lansbury
keyFigures.role: Led the Poplar council revolt of 1921 over rates and relief.

sources.title: Poplarism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Council minimum wage, equal pay, generous poor relief, rates equalisation and defiance of the courts.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Red Vienna ran public baths, school medical services and infant welfare centres, so adherents back public health provision, though the documented schemes were municipal rather than national. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Poplar paid council workers a minimum wage above the market rate and equal pay for women, which extends naturally to a higher general minimum. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement's whole premise is that water, gas, transport and housing are better run as public services than left to private firms.

public-ownership.rationale: Municipalisation of utilities, transport and other services is the movement's defining practice, as the article on it describes.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Breitner's Vienna taxed luxuries and funded housing with a progressive levy, and Italian socialist councils shifted taxes toward property.

unions-good.rationale: Municipal socialism combined public-service unions with co-operatives and tenant groups as its social base.

property-fundamental.rationale: Fabian writers treated land and capital as a common birthright and municipalised private undertakings, so property gives way to public purpose.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Its preferred remedy was taking over private monopolies rather than regulating them; tighter regulation is inferred as a fallback it would accept.

cut-welfare.rationale: Generous poor relief, school meals and child welfare were core outputs of municipal socialist councils such as Poplar.

worker-ownership.rationale: Co-operatives were allies, but the default owner was the municipality, not the workforce; adherents were not united on this.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No source covers it; inferred from the democratic-left, working-class tradition wary of police powers.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not an issue in the period; modern municipal socialists differ.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; adherents inferred to be split between speech liberties and anti-discrimination aims.

strong-leader.rationale: The Fabian approach relied on elected councils and majority votes, not leaders bypassing them.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement uses the local state as the instrument of reform and rejects abolishing it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left-reformist inclination toward public safety regulation.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; its spending priority was housing, health and services rather than police and army.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by historical municipal socialists; modern ones are divided.

decide-locally.rationale: Local government was the vehicle, but Poplar sought London-wide rate equalisation, so adherents want strong local powers without opposing national action.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its welfare and reform orientation.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents ranged from socially conservative Labour to progressive councils; no source settles it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the historic movement; modern municipal socialists generally support it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from left-wing social reform stance.

more-religion-public.rationale: Red Vienna's socialists tried to limit Catholic influence and clashed with the Church over cremation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a historic concern; modern municipal socialists generally support it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No source addresses it; adherents likely split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement was internationalist in networks but local in focus; it took no stand on national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Fabian municipal socialism sought gradual, practical reform through existing councils and parliament, rejecting sudden revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's internationalist socialist networks.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its cross-national socialist networks.

free-trade.rationale: The opened sources record no municipal socialist position on tariffs or trade; its concerns were local services, so neutral.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an internationalist labour outlook.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign military action lay outside municipal reform; no source gives a position and internationalist socialists divided on it.

open-borders.rationale: Never addressed; municipal socialists' focus was local welfare provision.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; its public-works programmes favoured growth but modern adherents split.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from willingness to use public power on collective problems.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Municipal gas, electricity and tramways show enthusiasm for technology delivered as public service; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates the movement; adherents' views on energy supply would divide between public-ownership and environmental concerns.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement was reformist and Lenin attacked it as a gradualist utopia; Fabians explicitly rejected revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Fabians valued expertise but also democratic control; no source settles the balance.

central-planning.rationale: Fabians favoured planning, but municipal socialists emphasised locally run services within mixed economies.

socialized-markets.rationale: Municipal enterprises sold services to the public while owned publicly, a market-compatible form of socialism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Fabian writers proposed land and death-duty taxes among several, not a single tax replacing the rest.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Clarke's Fabian essay proposed heavy death duties paid to municipalities.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; adherents prefer services and work provision over cash.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protection of national industry was not a municipal socialist issue, and no source takes a side.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Public enterprises and municipal works direct investment locally; strategic national direction is inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Favoured public over small-owner property; inferred from its collective ownership aims.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Councils set minimum wages for municipal workers, taking wage labour as given and aiming to improve it.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; its model is elected councils, not corporatist bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Municipal socialism operated through contested elections, often alongside liberals in coalition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Fabian democratic programme sought elected, accountable government; monarchy never defended.

democracy-best.rationale: Local electoral democracy is the means; Sesto Fiorentino even used a referendum on a municipal facility.

direct-votes.rationale: One documented use of a referendum; not a general demand.

workers-councils.rationale: Power was exercised through elected municipal councils within parliamentary systems.

right-to-secede.rationale: Vienna gained federal-state status in 1922, but no source states a secession principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Fabian Essays frame socialism as the culmination of the democratic ideal.

political-violence-never.rationale: Fabians held violence unlikely and unwise, but Poplar-style defiance shows adherents were not strictly pacifist.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from welfare and civic focus.

separate-church-state.rationale: Vienna's socialists curbed Catholic influence and fought the Church over cremation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Secular municipal governance, including the cremation dispute, rejected clerical authority.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from public provision of services.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from priority on social spending.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalist outlook.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fabians rejected Marxist class struggle while Austromarxists embraced it; adherents split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not stated; inferred from redistributive taxes and public housing.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land claims were not addressed by the movement, and nothing in its sources implies a stance.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations were not discussed by municipal socialists; modern adherents would likely split by tendency.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from local and class focus.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from collective provision ethos.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The movement stressed collective provision but never framed duties as outranking individual rights, so no clear answer.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; historic movement favoured parks but for public use.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is absent from municipal socialist sources; public-health councils focused on infant welfare, not limiting numbers.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Municipal gas, electricity and tramways embraced industrial infrastructure; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Municipal socialists welcomed utilities technology but not disruption of institutions; no source supports a position on speeding change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Biotechnology is anachronistic here and has no documented municipal socialist position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from emphasis on democratic control.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A modern digital-privacy issue with no connection to municipal socialist programmes, so left neutral.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Gas and water socialism was pragmatic, but adherents did hold an ideology; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Reform came mainly through winning council elections, though Poplar showed some defiance.

means-match-ends.rationale: Neither the sources nor the movement's practice state a view that methods must prefigure ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred; the movement was urban and industrial.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; its model of specialised public services implies not.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Poplar relief was set by need, but adherents did not claim a full communist principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Services were taken over from private firms to be run for public benefit rather than profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Fabian rent theory attacks unearned incomes but did not adopt Marx's exploitation claim; adherents vary.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Lenin criticised municipal socialism as reformist; adherents worked democratically.

collective-farming.rationale: Clarke proposed municipal land and co-operative farming for parish laborers, but not compulsory collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Reformist municipal socialists did not make a theory of imperialism central; Marxists in the wider movement did, so it is not a defining claim.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation financed public housing and services in Vienna and elsewhere.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal philosophy of state limits was not part of municipal socialism, whose adherents accepted broad public action beyond harm prevention but without stating a principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from collective provision focus.

conscription.rationale: Military service was not a municipal question, and no source gives a position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Municipal socialists put their faith in democratic voice through elected councils, so the claim that exit matters more is rejected by inference.

state-as-business.rationale: Services were run for public benefit, not as profit-driven customer businesses.

positive-liberty.rationale: Red Vienna aimed to give workers material means through housing, health and education.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source suggests municipal socialists blamed universities and media for political power; they focused on councils and wealth.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from egalitarian outlook.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; its model is territorial election.

total-state.rationale: Local reformists working within liberal democracy, with political parties competing.

national-rebirth.rationale: Municipal socialism was a gradual civic reform movement, not a project of national regeneration, so adherents are inferred to disagree.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Its programme was municipal and domestic, and its internationalist socialist networks imply opposition to expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Municipal socialism operated through elected councils and public law, so rule by personal oaths of lords and followers is contrary to its practice.

bound-labor.rationale: Its concern was improving wages and working conditions for free workers, so legally binding farmers to a lord is opposed by inference.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology is far from municipal socialist concerns; its reformers claimed pragmatic expertise, so no clear stance.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources discuss policy rather than moral philosophy; adherents ranged from religious to secular, so neutral.

single-common-good.rationale: Municipal socialists spoke of public welfare but also accepted competing party and class interests in elections, so no clear answer.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The movement's sources do not address Zionism, and adherents' views on it varied across eras.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No documented position; diaspora return rights were outside the movement's concerns.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival played no role in municipal socialism and no source addresses it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Public ownership implies a democratic voice for the public; workplace votes are inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Red Vienna expanded public kindergartens and schools; vouchers are inferred as disfavoured.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Breitner financed Vienna's programme from taxation rather than borrowing.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred from preference for public over private economic control.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from reliance on laws and public institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic principle.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic for a 19th and early 20th century local movement; no source on its views of UN authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular policy against Church influence suggests it; not stated.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist welfare ethos.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Poplar paid generous relief without harsh work tests, defying the national scale.

class-collaboration.rationale: Municipal socialism often worked with liberals yet rested on labour movement; adherents split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred; the movement built public parks and libraries.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western bloc building is not in municipal socialist sources and was not a feature of the movement.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Poplar's equal pay for women suggests rejection.

ban-interest.rationale: Municipal councils borrowed and, at Vienna, deliberately avoided borrowing, but no source shows a demand to ban interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed by sources, but the egalitarian, working-class politics of the movement is inferred to oppose it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Adherents saw local government as a usable instrument of reform, not only of class rule; Lenin criticised this.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy sourcing was framed in terms of municipal ownership of gas and electricity, not whether to expand fossil fuel production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Municipal socialist sources do not discuss immigrant assimilation; no stance is documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: This conspiracy narrative has no place in municipal socialist writings, which blame private monopolies rather than hidden plots.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; socialist parties generally favoured it.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a national model abroad conflicts with its local and internationalist outlook, though exchange between socialist cities was real.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Poplar equal pay suggests recognition; not stated.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Critics alleged patronage, but adherents defended honest civic government.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The opened sources record no such policy; the movement's public-health work targeted infant care and sanitation, so opposition is inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No source discusses prosecuting past abuses; accountability is inferred from the democratic-left outlook.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Directly opposed by municipal provision of services.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Nothing in municipal socialist sources supports it, and its egalitarian ethos implies rejection.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not stated but implicit in egalitarian socialism.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Municipal socialists built socialism city by city and never argued a one-country theory, so no position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement's sources do not address settler colonialism, though Australian and North American municipal socialism existed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law was not a municipal socialist issue, and no source gives a view.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Legal limits on changing religion conflict with the secular, rights-respecting politics of its councils, though no source addresses it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religious-nationalist cause with no connection to municipal socialism; no position recorded.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Red Vienna's Social Democrats pursued secular schooling; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This Soviet-era thesis is alien to a reformist movement that Lenin criticised, so inferred disagreement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Municipal socialism acted through elected councils and majority votes, which assumes legitimacy rests on consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export goals form no part of municipal socialism, and no source takes a position.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities contradicts the movement's welfare and democratic commitments, as inferred from its practice.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Absolute libertarian non-aggression is foreign to a movement that taxed and municipalised private property by law.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Municipal socialism rests on cooperative public provision, rejecting competition as the engine of improvement.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Austria's SDAP was itself banned in 1934, but no stated view on banning others.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not in the sources, but the movement's concern for workers' dependence is consistent with it.

separated-powers.rationale: Poplar defied court orders, but adherents did not reject checks in general.

vanguard-party.rationale: Lenin's critique of municipal reformism shows adherents rejected vanguard approach.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Poplar's relief programme and Vienna's priority housing put the poor first.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Councils were hurt by 1980s Thatcher limits; inferred opposition.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The movement combined with public-service unions, so legal limits on strikes and picketing would be opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Municipal socialists attributed poverty to housing, wages and institutions, which they sought to reform, not to numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nothing in its sources supports this claim, and its internationalist working-class outlook points the other way.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not in municipal socialist practice, which used elections to councils.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: No source speaks to emergency powers; democratic-left suspicion of executive power gives a mild inferred disagreement.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Fair-price municipal provision of bread and pharmacies in Italian councils suggests acceptance.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of media conflicts with the competitive electoral politics through which municipal socialism worked.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the armed forces is a Leninist idea absent from municipal socialism.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed in sources; the internationalist outlook implies opposition to long waits.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Fabians proposed paid members of Parliament but no source shows a wage cap, so adherents are split or indifferent.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline varied among councils and the sources do not say; no clear stance.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the armed forces plays no role in municipal socialism, and a local-democratic movement is inferred to prefer legislatures.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside municipal socialist concerns, apart from its conflicts with the Catholic Church in Vienna.

clerical-rule.rationale: Red Vienna's socialists opposed Catholic clerical influence.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Socialist networks differed on war in 1914; municipal socialist sources give no single answer.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Municipal socialists built libraries, parks and cultural facilities, which makes censorship for virtue unlikely.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Re-election limits were not an issue; municipal socialist mayors such as Hoan and Zeidler served many terms, but no principle is stated.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not documented; democratic accountability suggests mild support.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances were beyond municipal politics, and no source takes a side.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Red Vienna built tens of thousands of municipal rented flats with low rents.

people-in-arms.rationale: The armed-citizenry idea is not part of municipal socialism and no source supports it.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The movement was concerned with urban slums and city services, so it did not romanticise rural life.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Fabian and municipal reformers were often educated professionals who valued expertise, so they would not accept this claim.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural relativism is not discussed by municipal socialists, and no stance is documented.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in sources; welfare-minded labour reformers are inferred to lean against it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from progressive school reform in Vienna.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Red Vienna promoted secular public schooling against clerical influence, so teaching creationism is inferred as opposed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed by municipal socialist sources, and adherents' views would split between moralism and liberty.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed; its internationalist, residence-based city politics suggests disagreement.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not directly discussed, but support for public services for diverse working-class communities makes mild agreement likely.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents balance secular uniform law against minority protection.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about social conformity is not part of municipal socialist writing.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt politics lay beyond a municipal movement, and no source gives a view.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A colonial-era claim not made by municipal socialists in the sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting was not a municipal socialist demand; its method was reform within existing law.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Developmentalist authoritarianism is inconsistent with its democratic and electoral methods.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is not addressed, but redistribution from rich to poor at home suggests mild support abroad.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the early movement; the pacifist leaning of labour reformers suggests disagreement.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election methods are not within municipal socialist concerns.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed; municipal socialism concerned local finance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial disputes were not part of municipal socialism; the internationalist outlook implies compromise for peace.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Fabian Essays treat land and capital as a common inheritance and justify municipal takeover.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union was not a municipal socialist topic in the sources; adherents' views split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not in its sources; public health regulation was, but no stated position on scientific uncertainty.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is outside municipal socialist concerns, and the sources give no answer.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed by municipal socialist sources and not part of its agenda.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Vienna limited Catholic influence but no source on seizing church property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; it concerns constitutional design that municipal socialism left aside.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; though Vienna gained separate federal status peacefully, no principle is stated.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A one-country-two-systems question is outside the sources and municipal socialist concerns.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine kingship is opposed to the movement's democratic, secular councils.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Vienna's Breitner taxes and progressive housing levy show adherents favoured rates rising with ability to pay.

character-from-environment.rationale: Slum clearance and housing reform assume environment shapes people; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler above law conflicts with the movement's constitutional methods and its use of law to municipalise services.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is not addressed by municipal socialism; its focus was on urban public services.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical mixed constitution is not part of its sources; its proposals reformed Parliament toward democracy.

leader-cult.rationale: The movement was run by elected councils and civic institutions, not leader worship.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not discussed in its sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Debates about post-revolutionary class struggle were not part of municipal socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land was to be municipalised, not handed to farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a mild internationalist inference favours return rights.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims on territory because co-nationals live there conflict with the movement's internationalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion contradicts the secular, anti-clerical stance of Red Vienna's socialists.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering is contrary to its democratic and secular outlook.

common-currency.rationale: A shared currency is not a municipal socialist issue and no source takes a side.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Linguistic-kinship unions are not part of its programme; the movement's networks were class-based.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government in culture is not discussed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Diaspora strategy is not addressed in municipal socialist sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Austromarxists said yes, Fabians less so; split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Hostility to private monopoly motivated municipalisation, so breaking up concentrated economic power is mildly supported by inference.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not discussed; the sources don't settle it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Poplar clashed with courts, but no stated view.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas on public bodies are not documented in the historic movement, and adherents would vary.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs conflict with the movement's cross-border socialist networks.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred; fair-wage contracts for public works.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones is a communist theme absent from municipal socialism, which paid fair wages.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Contrasted with reformism by Lenin; Fabians rejected such approach.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Fabian Essays platform included democratic reform of Parliament and heavy death duties.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Curriculum emphasis is not discussed in sources; no stance is documented.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The tutelage of 'less advanced' societies is not discussed, but the movement's egalitarianism suggests rejection.

patriotic-education.rationale: Municipal socialist education programmes are not described as nationalistic, and its internationalism suggests scepticism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not a historic issue; adherents would be split between colour-blind and corrective views.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation was not a municipal socialist theme, and no source gives a position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Fabian gradualists thought capitalism could be reformed into socialism; Marxist adherents disagreed, so adherents are split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not discussed in its sources; internationalist socialists tended to reject imperial influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; the movement dealt with local public services and not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Critics said municipal jobs built a privileged layer; adherents reject.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Private discrimination rights are inconsistent with the equal public provision municipal councils offered.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights entrenchment is not discussed in its sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed by municipal socialist sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Municipal socialism won power through elections and treated democratic choice of rulers as basic.

minority-veto.rationale: Council government by majority vote conflicts with giving minorities a veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Poplar councillors defied a court, but no source supports a general doctrine of resisting rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Fabian socialists aimed to legislate socialism through Parliament and treated it as the sovereign lawmaker.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not discussed in sources; a mild inference from humanitarian reform orientation.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Favoured public entitlement over charity from the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement was civic activism through local politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school-style cultural critique is not part of municipal socialism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not part of its sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not a municipal socialist doctrine.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born conflicts with its working-class internationalism.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed; municipal socialism itself reflects national roads to socialism, but no principle is stated.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; no source speaks to development strategy.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentist demands are foreign to municipal socialism's civic focus.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Pre-colonial peoples' political leadership is not discussed in municipal socialist sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Red Vienna ended under Dollfuss, but no direct statement.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The condemnation of fascism and communism together is not a municipal socialist doctrine, and adherents would vary.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed in sources, though American municipal socialists were Progressive-era reformers who would reject this revision.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Disputes over monuments and flags are absent from its sources, so no position is drawn.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; no municipal socialist source gives a stance.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The seriousness of domestic violence by sex is not discussed in its sources.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Municipal socialism spread across cultures through socialist networks, which suggests no cultural-limit thesis.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armed forces guarding the constitution is contrary to its civic-democratic methods.

paid-care-work.rationale: Public child-care and welfare centres suggest it.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; family ethics lay outside municipal socialist programmes.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though Fabian administrators valued expertise.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed; municipal socialism concerned local ownership, not foreign firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mild inference from left social reform.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandates are a council-democracy idea; municipal socialism kept representative government, so no position.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Public provision, not private savings, is the movement's model for social insurance.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Clarke proposed municipal land acquisition and holding.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not documented, but Fabians favoured democratic budgeting through elected councils.

single-official-language.rationale: Official-language policy is not covered by municipal socialist sources.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign land ownership is not a municipal socialist theme.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Modern anti-discrimination doctrine is not addressed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; municipal socialists focused on provision of basic needs, not critique of consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; municipal socialism had no foreign policy.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power intervention is contrary to the movement's internationalism.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from distrust of private utility interests.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Controls on foreign NGO funding are a modern issue absent from the movement's sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth-rate incentives are not discussed, though Vienna's infant welfare packages show some family support.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; its internationalism suggests rejection.

job-guarantee.rationale: Clarke envisaged free and honorable municipal employment replacing charity.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed in its sources, and the movement offered no theory of international relations.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Poplar defied court orders, but adherents generally work through law.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; international politics lay beyond municipal socialism.

industrial-unions.rationale: Craft versus industrial unionism is not addressed by the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy charges against a minority have no basis in municipal socialist writing and contradict its egalitarian outlook.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed in municipal socialist sources.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not documented; democratic accountability suggests mild support.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; local ownership of services is not the same as local sourcing of goods.

informal-organisation.rationale: Municipal socialists organised through parties and councils, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed by municipal socialist sources.

religious-nation.rationale: Defining nationhood by religion conflicts with its secular and class politics.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Ritual submission to a leading power has no place in its politics.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Poplar demanded equalisation of rates across London.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Municipalisation targeted production and utilities, not personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Lenin attacked municipal socialism, but adherents did not typically advocate defeating communism; mild inferred disagreement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The movement replaced private providers with public ones.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx's formula was not municipal socialist doctrine; religious and secular socialists were both present.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed by the opened sources; Fabians viewed capitalism as having created industrial resources, inferred mild agreement.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Poplar paid equal wages to women, but no source frames women's equality as requiring wider economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Vienna expanded public kindergartens, lunches and child welfare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism played no part in municipal socialism, whose concerns were services and wages.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations inside a state are not a municipal socialist concern.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Co-operatives were allies of the movement, but small self-governing communities were not its model; cities and councils were.

majority-settlement.rationale: Settling a majority group in minority regions is nationalist demographic policy foreign to the movement's class politics.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way positioning is not stated by municipal socialists, who considered themselves socialists.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing historical land claims are outside its sources and concerns.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; nothing in the movement supports denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the historic sources; modern municipal socialists reject it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Municipal socialism won elections competitively and is inferred to oppose suppression.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Its secular, anti-clerical stance in Vienna implies opposition.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; socialist internationalism implies rejection.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious obligations of armed resistance fall outside the movement entirely, so only a mild inferred disagreement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Its secular councils reject religious tests for rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Referendums on municipal facilities and tenant groups suggest support for popular participation, though the movement was mainly representative.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional theory is not part of its sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed historically; modern municipal socialists generally support it.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life law is not discussed in historic municipal socialist sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Municipal socialists were explicitly on the left and not seeking to transcend it.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's alienation concept is not central to municipal socialist reform sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; nothing in the movement supports it and its internationalism implies rejection.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Its authority came from elections, and Vienna's socialists resisted Church claims.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; secular-minded adherents would be split on regulation of religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in sources; labour-protection orientation suggests mild support.

social-market-economy.rationale: A mixed market with social protection is close to some municipal socialism, but adherents wanted public ownership beyond that, so neutral.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though labour pacifists supported disarmament.

rich-first.rationale: Municipal socialism sought broad distribution of services, not allowing some to grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Bloc politics postdate its heyday and no source gives an answer.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession is incompatible with its elected-council form.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit is a co-operative idea not found in the sources on municipal socialism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not addressed directly, but resistance to central-state limits on spending shaped the 1980s urban left.

property-franchise.rationale: Fabian Essays platform proposed adult suffrage.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is not part of municipal socialism.

reification.rationale: Lukacs's concept is not a municipal socialist theme.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a mild inference from socialist critique of wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Municipal socialists governed through published bylaws and statutes, so public standing law is implicitly supported.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racially limited suffrage conflicts with its adult-suffrage democratic programme.

online-participation.rationale: An internet-era idea not addressed by its sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; municipal accountability suggests mild support.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Its secular, egalitarian politics imply rejection.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Discriminatory boycotts have no support in its sources.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed in its sources; it used elected councils, not sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious doctrine was not a municipal socialist concern.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Fabians taxed unearned wealth because of its social effects, though the liberty framing is not stated.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed historically; modern municipal socialists back it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Vienna curbed clerical influence but did not push atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Police and prisons are not targeted by the sources; municipal socialism sought to expand public institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociationalism is not addressed in its sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Poplar replaced charity with public relief, and Clarke saw public employment replacing charity.

term-limits.rationale: Limits on terms in office are not discussed, and long-serving socialist mayors existed.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not part of municipal socialism.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern concern not addressed in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious office is not a municipal socialist concern.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not addressed directly; Poplar's equal pay for women suggests mild agreement.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; local democracy and inclusion suggest mild support.

rent-control.rationale: Low rents in municipal housing; rent caps inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyright are not discussed in its sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Uniformed state youth drill is contrary to civic and welfare-focused socialism; Red Vienna's youth work was voluntary.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic for the early movement; later labour councils declared nuclear-free zones, but this is not in the sources, so low.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is a question of national defence policy, which municipal socialist sources never address.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal genocide recognition lies outside municipal socialist concerns, and no source gives a stance.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Fabian writers taxed rent and unearned incomes.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism was a minority view among labour reformers.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Primordial national continuity is not part of municipal socialist thought.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Theories of sex and gender construction are absent from its sources, so no position is documented.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory debates over the category of women do not appear in municipal socialist sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: National martyr cults are not part of municipal socialism.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Municipal socialism was pragmatic civic reform, not a spiritual contest.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora-homeland ties are not among its concerns, and its sources give no position.

culture-before-state.rationale: Municipal socialists sought state power locally first, so no cultural-renewal-first claim.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology of divine language was not a municipal socialist matter, so neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist reading of scripture is not discussed by the municipal socialist sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic ownership aims conflict with its class-based programme.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging administrative regions around one people is not a theme of municipal socialism.

independent-unions.rationale: Public-service unions were allies, but independence from labour parties and councils is not discussed, so mild inference.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from working-class parties governing cities.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water, gas, transport and local services in public hands is the core demand.

second-chamber.rationale: The Fabian parliamentary reforms in the sources do not address upper chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal socialists made the town council the owner of gas, water, trams and housing, but Fabians and social democrats also backed national ownership of other industries, which the statement rules out.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Socialist networks spread municipal socialism, but confederations were not its stated form.

family-wage.rationale: Poplar's minimum wages for council workers hint at a living wage; family wage not stated.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation speed is not discussed in its sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Longevity research is anachronistic and not addressed, so no position can be drawn.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment privacy is a digital-era issue not addressed by municipal socialism.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online pseudonymity is a modern issue with no connection to the movement's sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Not addressed in sources, though municipal socialism's social focus gives a mild inferred agreement that the state serves people.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources do not take a view on human spirituality; adherents ranged from religious to secular.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Vienna and Poplar suffered federal override and cuts, and adherents resisted it.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is not addressed by the movement, so neutral.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban public housing favours dense cities; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race-based organising conflicts with its class-based politics.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not discussed by municipal socialists; adherents would split between universalist and identity-based views.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed in its sources; labour reformers broadly endorsed defensive-only force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Language-based definitions of nationhood are not addressed in municipal socialist sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate electorates by community conflict with its class and territorial franchise.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy claims about foreign partition are not in its sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Red Vienna expanded free medical and school provision, so free higher education is a mild inference.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pollution taxation is not in its sources, though it endorsed taxes on unearned income.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed; mild inference from planning of public infrastructure.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The claim that women bring distinct values is not stated in its sources, though Poplar paid women equal wages.

arms-reduction.rationale: Labour reformers generally supported arms limits, but no source speaks to it here.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed in sources; democratic accountability suggests mild support.

capital-controls.rationale: Controls on capital movement are national policy and unaddressed in municipal socialist sources.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Leaving money to the market contradicts the movement's preference for public over market provision, though central banking itself is not discussed in its sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is outside the movement's municipal focus and the sources give no stance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the movement's constitutional, democratic character; armed groups are not discussed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed; individual socialist councillors and Labour figures differed on war resistance.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Municipal socialists worked in alliance with unions and, as at Poplar, set council wages above market rates, favouring collectively agreed pay.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic; municipal socialists preferred fair wages and public provision to tax-system top-ups, but there is no stated position.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Socialist councils repeatedly clashed with national limits on local raising and spending, such as Poplar's defiance and 1980s rate-capping.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic rules lie outside the local-government focus; no stated position.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement is reformist and democratic, working through elected councils; Lenin criticised it for just this reason.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's local autonomy, with councils trying municipal ownership, co-operatives and other arrangements without a single national blueprint.

sacred-nation.rationale: The tradition is civic and local, with a socialist internationalist outlook; inferred as no sacred nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's support for free public education and welfare provision.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Councils resisted a centre that limited their powers, but the colonial analogy is not in the sources; split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Fabian and Christian socialist adherents differ.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to public ownership of services and public education; broadcasting postdates much of the tradition.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; Red Vienna clashed with the Church while Christian and secular socialists coexisted, so neutral is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The tradition concerned urban services; support for farm prices is not documented, so neutral is inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The 1980s urban left declared nuclear-free council zones, and inferred from that and the existing answers on deterrents, adherents lean against keeping weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: Municipal socialism was carried out by labour and social-democratic parties such as Poplar Labour and the Vienna Social Democrats, who stood independently of the established parties. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from Poplar's equal pay for women and the tradition's reformist egalitarianism; FGM itself is not addressed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Poplar's equal pay for women and the Fabian suffrage and equality demands; inheritance is not addressed directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition, so neutral is inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Councils preferred public regulation and provision of services over private litigation; inferred, since pollution liability is not discussed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Red Vienna and the Fabians worked through elected councils and parliaments, so unelected chiefs having a lawmaking role is inferred to be rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; councils took public health and sanitation measures but no priority over liberty is documented, so neutral is inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Poplarism's generous and humane relief and the reformist temper suggest opposition to fixed punitive terms; inferred, not stated.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; councils ran schools and services but language requirements for immigrants are not documented, so neutral is inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Municipal socialists worked closely with unions and fair-wage policy, so compulsory dues are not objectionable to them; inferred from the union alliances described in the article.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition stresses widening participation, as with Fabian and Poplar support for wider suffrage, so extra hurdles to voting are opposed; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Red Vienna clashed with the Church and favoured secular public institutions, which implies equal legal standing for all; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Fabian and municipal socialists saw democracy as extending into economic life through public ownership, not just elections; inferred from Fabian Essays.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; the secular, reformist urban left of Red Vienna and the London County Council is inferred to accept it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; elected local government accountable to residents makes arbitrary cutting of communications unacceptable. Inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The tradition prefers direct public provision of services, housing and relief to a single cash payment; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Fabian Essays and the councils backed suffrage widening, and Poplar paid equal pay to women, so equal political rights are accepted.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; Red Vienna opposed Church power but the movement had no shared view on religion and women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the egalitarian, reformist outlook.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Poplar's equal pay policy shows support for public action on equality, though dedicated agencies are not documented; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the aim of taking local services into public ownership: adherents would hold that shared resources belong to the community rather than to whoever claims them first.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reformist, internationally minded socialism; its sources do not discuss international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from Red Vienna's conflict with the Church and the movement's secular public provision of health and education; the sources do not address scripture.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from Poplarism's equal pay and the movement's democratic egalitarianism; its sources do not discuss self-government of national groups.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's gradual, democratic route and its rejection of revolutionary Marxism, which makes defending a bureaucratically ruled planned state unlikely.

indirect-election.rationale: The movement worked through directly elected councils and wider suffrage, so rule by delegates chosen by lower councils is inferred to be unattractive.

national-church-status.rationale: Red Vienna clashed with the Church, and the movement's secular public services imply equal treatment of religions; inferred, not directly stated.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the movement's belief in devolved local self-government; its sources say nothing about ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the democratic, consent-based principles of the tradition; its sources do not address disputed territories.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The tradition never addressed colonial borders and adherents have no common position, so this is left neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the movement's aim of raising living standards through public provision, which sits poorly with limiting needs as an ideal; not directly addressed.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the movement's general egalitarian universalism; its sources do not discuss indigenous homelands.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Poplarism's equal pay and the tradition's egalitarianism; conscription was not a theme of the sources.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: the movement is about civic services and municipal self-government, not national ancestral claims.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic, rule-bound reformism; killing without trial is not discussed.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign policy is outside municipal socialism; no stated position.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: a locally focused democratic movement with no concern for kin abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Fabian Essays propose that land rents and municipal land ownership return value to the community.

self-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed collective provision but also personal liberty, so adherents are not clearly pointed either way.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: Red Vienna funded services through progressive taxes on luxuries and property rather than on everyday goods.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Municipal services such as water, transport, health and schools were open to all residents rather than means-tested.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The movement works through council elections and alliances with unions, co-operatives and tenant groups, so organised groups are central.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to private monopolies and its council contracts at fair wages; sources do not state this.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: Red Vienna clashed with the Church, and the movement's civic politics is not denominational.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favoured modern public works but says nothing on ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from Red Vienna's progressive social reforms; not documented in the sources.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: the movement wanted public control of utilities, but it concerns local rather than national resources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Red Vienna's progressive taxation and Poplarism's rates equalisation aimed to correct unequal outcomes, not to accept them.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anachronistic and not discussed in the sources.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: a labour-aligned movement in which class inequality, not racism, is the central concern; the sources do not discuss it.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Poplarism's councillors defied the courts and government to pay minimum wages and relief, showing willingness to put justice above the law; the sources do not state a doctrine.

multipolar-world.rationale: Not addressed; the movement concerned domestic local government.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Not addressed; the Fabians drew on diverse value theories, so adherents' view cannot be sourced.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Not addressed; adherents combined civic pride with internationalist labour ties.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: Poplarism and council housing put wages, relief and living standards first; identity issues are not discussed.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The movement is gradual and democratic, explicitly excluding the revolutionary Marxism Lenin counterposed to it.

missingStatements.text: Local councils should be free to set their own tax rates and spend as they choose, without national government limits.
missingStatements.rationale: Socialist councils repeatedly clashed with national governments over powers to raise and spend money, and Thatcher's limits are said to have ended the movement's 1980s phase.

missingStatements.text: Local government should build and own housing to rent to ordinary households at low rents.
missingStatements.rationale: Red Vienna built over 60,000 municipal flats with low rents, and municipal housing and slum clearance recur across the movement.

notes: Revolutionary Marxists such as Lenin rejected the strategy as gradualism; Poplarism shows a more confrontational wing. Most answers outside public services, taxation, welfare and democracy are inferences.
